The Engine of the Bootstrap

Source: R/bootstrap_engine.R
bootstrap_engine.Rd

Draws resampled data sets from a fit, refits the model on each and returns the coefficients of the replicates that were kept. It is the engine that add_bootstrap() and the predictive bootstrap of pred_bootstrap() share.

Usage

bootstrap_engine(
  object,
  n,
  resample,
  refit,
  seed = NULL,
  aside = NULL,
  replace = TRUE,
  validate = TRUE,
  hook = NULL,
  batch = NULL,
  stream = TRUE,
  adjust = TRUE,
  check = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

The StatmodFit().

n

The number of replicates to keep.

resample

A resample_method object.

refit

"coefficients" or "full".

seed

NULL, or the value of .Random.seed from which the stream continues.

aside

The rows of random_modes() whose effects are redrawn by a parametric replicate; NULL for all of them.

replace

TRUE replaces a failed replicate by the next draw; FALSE makes exactly n draws and leaves the failures out.

validate

TRUE applies the mode error and the identification criteria; FALSE fails a replicate on an error only.

hook

NULL, or a function of a refit and its position that is called in the calling process for every replicate kept.

batch

The largest number of draws made before their refits run; NULL draws all that are missing.

stream

TRUE manages the state of the random number generator of the session as described above.

adjust

TRUE stores a random-effect coordinate of a parametric replicate as \(\hat b^* - b^* + \hat b\).

check

TRUE rejects the fits that the bootstrap does not handle.

Value

A list with coefficients (a matrix with a row for each replicate kept), hyper (a matrix, or NULL), status (an integer for every draw), seed_start, seed_end, random, raw (the matrix of the random-effect coefficients of the replicates as refitted, without the adjustment of the random effects, for a parametric scheme with adjust = TRUE beside random effects, and NULL otherwise) and raw_cols (the positions of the columns of raw among the columns of coefficients).

Details

The draws are made in the calling process, one replicate after another from the random number stream, and the refits go to worker_map() with the number of workers that the fit carries. A replicate is therefore a function of its position in the stream and not of the number of workers, and the first n replicates of a stream are those of a run of n. The state of .Random.seed after the last replicate that was kept is returned, so that a later call continues the stream: 500 replicates followed by 300 more are the 800 replicates of one run from the same seed. A refit does not draw from the stream of the calling process: the seed is saved before it and restored after it.

A replicate fails when the refit signals an error (status 1), when the mode error of the refit exceeds mode_error_limit() (status 2), or when a coefficient is unidentified in the replicate and not in the fit (status 3), which is the case of a level of a factor whose observations have all a zero weight. The information of the mode error is that of the inner fit. A failed replicate is replaced by the next draw of the stream with replace = TRUE, and the engine stops with an error when the failures outnumber the successes after at least ten draws.

See also

add_bootstrap(), predictive_bootstrap(), worker_map()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(40))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(40, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
eng <- statmodels7:::bootstrap_engine(fit, 5, case_resample(),
                                      "coefficients")
dim(eng$coefficients)
#> [1] 5 3
